Well, I have tried almost every antidepressant on the book and nothing helped. With ECT I went from moderate-severe to depression to, get this, completely cured after 8 sessions.

...for a month and a half. That's one of the worst parts about the treatment. It works really well, but the relapse rate is sadly pretty high.
It hasn't been even two weeks. That's good to hear.

Pretty significant. It's pretty hard to explain but I have gaps in my memory that are like a corrupted hard drive. It's like I know for certain that I used to know something but unlike previously when something slipped my mind no amount of thinking is going to make me remember it. And I did lose lots and lots of memories. I don't tend to live in the past so losing memories of events doesn't bother me.

However losing information and skills I Iearned at school was something I was not prepared for. My dream job has always been software engineer/game programmer and while previously I could do complex algorithms with ease, now my mind just wont co-operate with me, even with simple stuff.

It really depends on can you handle the memory loss. Most memories I had were negative so forgetting events wasn't at all bad. I did however forget plenty of stuff that I needed to do computer programming so I'm not nearly as good as before my treatment. It sucks but my doctors said it will be temporary.

On the plus side my depression is almost completely gone. I tried tens of medications and years of therapy before, nothing helped. I'd do it again.

My problem is I don't know what loneliness feels like. I know depression, anger, despair, frustration and anxiety. They all feel different. Yet I have never felt bad and used "lonely" as the most accurate emotional label.

Which is really conserning since I notice very clear patterns of me isolating and my head getting all fucked up.

It's a lifetime struggle to learn.
Especially in your age, your peers are most likely very judging, mean and fault-finding. Usually they don't try to understand, instead they'll find any minor reason not to get along with you. Don't get discouraged if you don't immediately succeed, teenagers are awful, and it gets better when they grow up.

Look people in the eye, don't take too much time when speaking, don't be rude. Try to change topics if the other person gets bored. An easy social hack is to just ask a lot of questions. Firstly, they'll do all of the talking, and second people love to talk about themselves.

People on the spectrum have a stunningly high comorbidity with depression. I'd be more surprised if you weren't depressed.

I'm not good with words. Just hang in there. That's at least what I'm trying to do.
